description: Scaffold the Tauri shell and the React/TypeScript (Vite) frontend, wired end-to-end through one placeholder command `app_version`, plus the frontend baseline vitest test (tasks.md P0.3, P0.4, and the frontend portion of P0.5). Depends on FEAT-001 (workspace must exist). Because the sandbox is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, tauri-app cannot be compiled offline (needs the `tauri` crate) and the frontend cannot `npm install`/run vitest offline; those verifications are gated to CI and must be documented as unverified-locally, NOT reported as passing.
steps: Tauri shell (P0.3): create crates/tauri-app/tauri.conf.json (Tauri v2 config: productName, version, identifier e.g. com.agentharbor.app, build.frontendDist pointing at ../../frontend/dist, build.devUrl http://localhost:5173, app.windows with one window, bundle config). Create crates/tauri-app/capabilities/default.json granting the webview least-privilege access to only the `app_version` command (Tauri v2 capability format: identifier, windows: ["main"], permissions listing core defaults plus the app_version command). Create src/main.rs (builds the tauri::Builder, registers AppState via .manage(), registers the app_version command via generate_handler!, runs). Create src/commands.rs with `#[tauri::command] pub fn app_version() -> String` returning env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(). Create src/state.rs with an `AppState` struct (Arc-wrapped placeholder subsystems; for Phase 0 it can be an empty or minimal struct with a #[derive(Default)]). Create src/events.rs with a placeholder core-event-to-emit bridge function stub. Wire main.rs to reference commands, state, events modules. Add crates/tauri-app/build.rs invoking tauri_build::build().

Frontend (P0.4): create frontend/ with package.json (name, private:true, scripts: dev=vite, build=tsc && vite build, test=vitest run, deps: react, react-dom, @tauri-apps/api; devDeps: vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, vitest, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom, jsdom, @types/react, @types/react-dom). Create frontend/index.html, frontend/vite.config.ts (react plugin, test config with environment jsdom, server.port 5173), frontend/tsconfig.json. Create frontend/src/main.tsx (React root render of App). Create frontend/src/app.tsx (App component that calls the typed IPC wrapper to fetch app_version and renders it). Create empty feature folders with a placeholder index.ts each: frontend/src/features/{chat,model-selector,tool-manager,agent-editor,history}/. Also create the other Section 3.2 frontend dirs as placeholders: src/state/ (conversations.ts, providers.ts, tools.ts, personas.ts placeholders), src/components/, src/types/.

Typed IPC stubs (P0.4): create frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts exporting a typed `appVersion(): Promise<string>` wrapper over `invoke('app_version')` from @tauri-apps/api/core. Create frontend/src/ipc/events.ts with typed listener stubs over the Tauri event API (e.g. a `listen`-based helper) even if no events are emitted yet in Phase 0 — provide the typed shape so later phases extend it.

Frontend baseline test (P0.5): add frontend/src/app.test.tsx using vitest + React Testing Library that renders <App /> and asserts it renders (mock @tauri-apps/api/core `invoke` so app_version resolves to a test value; assert the value appears). This test must be structured to pass under `vitest run` (verified in CI, not offline).

Add frontend/.gitignore (node_modules, dist) and ensure frontend/package-lock.json will be committed when generated in CI. Document in the feature findings that npm install + vitest run could not be executed offline.

Local verification: run `cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo build && cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` to confirm FEAT-001's baseline is still green after adding files (tauri-app remains excluded from default-members). Do NOT attempt `cargo build -p tauri-app`, `tauri dev`, `tauri build`, `npm install`, or `vitest` offline — they require network/registries/CLI absent from the sandbox; record them as CI-gated / unverified-locally in findings with the exact reason.
acceptance_criteria: crates/tauri-app contains tauri.conf.json, capabilities/default.json, build.rs, and src/{main.rs,commands.rs,state.rs,events.rs}, matching architecture.md Section 3.2.

A single placeholder `#[tauri::command] app_version` exists in commands.rs and is registered in main.rs's generate_handler!, and capabilities/default.json grants only that command (plus required core defaults).

frontend/ contains package.json, vite.config.ts, index.html, tsconfig.json, src/main.tsx, src/app.tsx, the five empty feature folders (chat, model-selector, tool-manager, agent-editor, history), src/ipc/commands.ts, src/ipc/events.ts, and the state/components/types placeholder dirs per Section 3.2.
src/ipc/commands.ts exposes a typed wrapper that invokes 'app_version'; src/app.tsx consumes it.
frontend/src/app.test.tsx is a vitest + RTL test that renders App with a mocked invoke and asserts the rendered app_version value (CI-runnable).
The offline Rust baseline (cargo build/test/clippy over default-members) remains green after these additions.
Feature findings clearly list what was verified locally vs what is CI-gated (tauri-app compile, tauri dev/build, npm install, vitest) with the INTEGRATIONS_ONLY reason.
verification: Confirm presence and shape of tauri-app files and frontend files via reading them; confirm app_version is the single registered command and capabilities/default.json scopes to it
findings:
Implemented the Tauri v2 shell and the React/TS (Vite) frontend, wired end-to-end through the single placeholder command `app_version`, plus the CI-runnable vitest baseline test. All files reproduce architecture.md Section 3.2 exactly.

TAURI SHELL (crates/tauri-app/): 
- tauri.conf.json: Tauri v2 format ($schema schema.tauri.app/config/2), productName 'Agent Harbor', version 0.1.0, identifier com.agentharbor.app, build.frontendDist ../../frontend/dist, build.devUrl http://localhost:5173, one window labeled 'main', bundle.active true.
- capabilities/default.json: Tauri v2 capability, identifier 'default', windows ["main"], permissions ["core:default", "core:app:allow-app-version"] — least privilege: only the app_version command plus required core defaults.
- build.rs: calls tauri_build::build().
- src/commands.rs: exactly one `#[tauri::command] pub fn app_version() -> String` returning env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string().
- src/state.rs: `#[derive(Debug, Default)] pub struct AppState {}` (minimal Arc-friendly placeholder).
- src/events.rs: placeholder core-event->emit bridge (CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL const + forward_core_event stub using tauri::Emitter).
- src/main.rs: builds tauri::Builder, .manage(AppState::default()), .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![commands::app_version]), .run(tauri::generate_context!()); declares mod commands/state/events.

FRONTEND (frontend/): package.json (private, scripts dev=vite, build='tsc && vite build', test='vitest run'; deps react, react-dom, @tauri-apps/api; devDeps vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, vitest, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom, jsdom, @types/react, @types/react-dom), index.html, vite.config.ts (react plugin, test.environment jsdom, server.port 5173, setupFiles test-setup.ts), tsconfig.json. src/main.tsx (React root render of <App/>), src/app.tsx (App calls the typed appVersion() IPC wrapper via useEffect and renders it in a data-testid=app-version span). Empty feature folders with placeholder index.ts each: src/features/{chat,model-selector,tool-manager,agent-editor,history}/. Section 3.2 placeholder dirs: src/state/{conversations,providers,tools,personas}.ts, src/components/index.ts, src/types/index.ts. src/test-setup.ts imports @testing-library/jest-dom.

TYPED IPC: src/ipc/commands.ts exports `appVersion(): Promise<string>` over invoke('app_version') from @tauri-apps/api/core. src/ipc/events.ts exports CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL, a CoreEvent type, and onCoreEvent() listener helper over @tauri-apps/api/event listen (typed shape for later phases).

BASELINE TEST: src/app.test.tsx (vitest + RTL) mocks @tauri-apps/api/core invoke to resolve 'app_version' -> '9.9.9-test', renders <App/>, asserts the value renders (getByTestId app-version) and invoke was called with 'app_version'. Structured to pass under `vitest run` in CI.

frontend/.gitignore ignores node_modules and dist (package-lock.json NOT ignored; it is generated+committed in CI). No node_modules committed.

DESIGN NOTE: kept FEAT-001's arrangement where crates/tauri-app is under `[workspace] exclude` (not `members`) so offline cargo commands stay green — did not change the workspace manifest.

VERIFIED LOCALLY (from /projects/agent-harbor/hybrid-orchestrator, all PASS, offline INTEGRATIONS_ONLY):
- `cargo build` -> Finished (6 lib crates, no registry contact; tauri-app excluded).
- `cargo test` -> 6 smoke tests pass (1 per lib crate), doc-tests 0.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` -> Finished, no errors.
- `cargo fmt --check` -> clean (exit 0).
The offline Rust baseline from FEAT-001 remains green after adding these files.

CI-GATED / NOT VERIFIABLE OFFLINE (documented, NOT attempted as passing; reason: network mode INTEGRATIONS_ONLY — crates.io and registry.npmjs.org return HTTP 403, Tauri CLI absent):
- `cargo build -p tauri-app` — needs the external `tauri`/`serde`/`serde_json` crates + tauri-build from crates.io (unreachable offline). Source written per Tauri v2 conventions; compiles in CI.
- `tauri dev` / `tauri build` — Tauri CLI not installed and cannot be installed; also needs network + display.
- `npm install` / `npm ci` — registry.npmjs.org blocked (403).
- `vitest run` (frontend/src/app.test.tsx) — requires npm install first; runs in CI where network exists. Written to pass but not executed locally.
Note: NODE_OPTIONS=--require .../proxy-bootstrap.js would break node invocations anyway; frontend tooling is entirely CI-gated.

REVIEW FIXES (2026-09-06-042215-review.md, addressed on branch phase-0-scaffold):
1. Missing Tauri bundle icons: generated valid placeholder icon files at crates/tauri-app/icons/ (32x32.png, 128x128.png, 128x128@2x.png as RGBA PNGs; icon.ico as 32x32 32bpp BMP-in-ICO; icon.icns embedding 128x128+256x256 PNGs via ic07/ic08). Verified structurally valid (PNG chunk CRCs, ICO/ICNS containers, `file` reports correct types). Cannot run `tauri icon` offline (no CLI/network); added icons/README.md marking them as placeholders to be regenerated from real branding. tauri.conf.json bundle.icon left referencing all five (all now exist).
2. Frontend lockfile/npm cache on first CI run: removed `cache: npm` + `cache-dependency-path` from the setup-node step in .github/workflows/ci.yml (setup-node errors hard when the lockfile is absent). The install step keeps `npm ci || npm install` so the first networked run generates the lockfile via `npm install`. Documented the re-enable-cache/switch-to-`npm ci` exit path in the workflow comment and the README lockfile policy (also clarified package-lock.json does not exist yet).
3. Capability permission: removed the misleading `core:app:allow-app-version` from capabilities/default.json (that gates Tauri's built-in app plugin, not the custom command). Custom `#[tauri::command]` handlers are authorized purely by registration in generate_handler! (main.rs). default.json now lists only `core:default` with a description explaining the real Tauri v2 authorization model (architecture.md Section 9.2). Fixed the stale doc comment in commands.rs that claimed the command was allowlisted in the capability file.
4. tauri-app `[workspace] exclude` decoupling: re-inclusion into `members` requires a networked Cargo.lock and cannot be done offline. Strengthened documentation of the tradeoff and concrete exit path in both hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml (in-code comment) and README.md so it is tracked rather than silently severed.

Re-verified offline Rust baseline after the fixes (from hybrid-orchestrator/, INTEGRATIONS_ONLY): cargo fmt --all --check clean, cargo build Finished, cargo test 6/6 smoke tests pass, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean. All changed JSON validated as parseable; ci.yml checked (no tabs, cache lines only in comments).
